newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW--Otsuka Kagu expects 60 pct profit rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Otsuka Kagu expects 60 pct profit rise.

text.p: Otsuka Kagu Ltd, a leading Japanese retailer of imported furniture, said it would record a 60 percent jump in its current profit to 6.4 billion yen this calendar year on buoyant sales.

"Looking at business conditions from January to April, it is certain we will revise upward our earlier earnings forecast estimates," Katsuhisa Otsuka, the company's president, told Reuters in a recent interview.
"It's my feeling that our current profit will grow 60 percent to 6.4 billion yen," he said.
In February, the firm predicted a current profit of 5.54 billion yen for calendar 1997, up 38.1 percent from the year before.
Otsuka said that although the firm's sales slid 44 percent in the first week of April after Japan raised its sales tax, they would be back to normal later this month and start growing again in May.
Otsuka Kagu operates membership-based sales outlets and has Japan's largest furniture showroom. Its shares were registered on the over-the-counter market in 1980.
The company's shares traded at 8,700 yen at Tokyo midday on Friday, up from Thursday's close of 8,600.
Otsuka said the rush of consumer buying prior to the sales-tax increase was more than enough to offset the damage the company suffered after the increase was implemented.

The company recorded year-on-year sales growth of 36 percent in January and 56 percent in February, followed by a 2.3-fold increase in March, when a record number of customers visited its outlets, Otsuka said.

The company plans to open two new stores later this year while continuing to scrap small outlets, he said. The number of Otsuka Kagu outlets has declined to 11 from a peak of 24, but total sales floor space has grown to its highest ever, he added.
